1	---
2	name: entity-resolution
3	description: Match a person, company, project, or concept a source or note refers to against existing knowledge-base entities — confident match, no match, or ambiguous. Use before adding a link, a stub page, or a frontmatter reference to any entity.
4	skill_api: 1
5	---
6	
7	# entity-resolution
8	
9	This skill answers one narrow question: **does this referenced entity
10	correspond to an existing knowledge-base page, and if not, does it warrant
11	one?** It does not decide which links a note should carry, how many, or
12	where they go — that judgment belongs to `entity-enrichment`. Keep the two
13	separate:
14	
15	```text
16	entity-resolution → determine what an entity refers to
17	entity-enrichment → decide how the note should connect to it
18	```
19	
20	If you're asking "what page is this?", you're in this skill. If you're
21	asking "should this note link to it, and how?", you're past this skill's
22	scope — hand the resolution result to `entity-enrichment`.
23	
24	## When to use
25	
26	- Any time a note, source, or edit mentions a person, company, project, or
27	  concept and you need to know whether it already has a page before
28	  proposing a link, a stub, or a frontmatter `ref` field.
29	- Most directly during `note-revision` and manual editing — anywhere an
30	  agent is touching a note by hand, outside `wakil enrich`.
31	
32	## The CLI path already does this — don't duplicate it
33	
34	`wakil enrich <source-id>` runs entity resolution as a fixed DAG step,
35	always invoked, never optional (`src/wakil/app/ingest_service.py`,
36	`_run_entity_resolution`) — `ingest-source` documents how that internal DAG
37	step fits into the pipeline. It applies the same judgment against every
38	entity the extraction step surfaced, then `_build_stub_entities` turns each
39	`action: create` result into a schema-routed stub page, and
40	`validate_proposal()` hard-stops on any entity type the schema doesn't
41	recognize rather than best-guessing a shape. If you're driving ingestion
42	through `wakil ingest` / `wakil enrich`, that mechanism already applies this
43	judgment — don't re-run it by hand.
44	
45	This skill exists for everywhere else: `note-revision`, ad hoc editing, or
46	any other case where an agent is resolving an entity mention outside that
47	pipeline. The judgment below is the same one the CLI's internal DAG step
48	encodes — apply it consistently so a note edited by hand and a note
49	produced by `wakil enrich` don't disagree about whether "Jane" is
50	`people/jane-doe.md`.
51	
52	## Decision procedure
53	
54	For each entity a source or note touches, resolve independently — one
55	transcript or note routinely touches several entities (a person, their
56	company, a project) at once; don't collapse them into one destination.
57	Reach exactly one of three outcomes:
58	
59	- **Confident match.** An existing page corresponds to this entity. Match
60	  by identity, not string equality: "Jane," "Jane Doe," and a stored
61	  `people/jane-doe.md` with `aliases: [Jane]` are the same person if
62	  context supports it. Point at the page's exact path; do not restate or
63	  guess at its frontmatter.
64	- **No match, and it clears the notability gate.** No page exists yet, but
65	  the entity is worth one — see below. Surface this as a create candidate
66	  for `entity-enrichment` to act on; don't create the page yourself as a
67	  side effect of resolving identity.
68	- **No match, and it doesn't clear the gate, or it's genuinely
69	  ambiguous.** A drive-by mention, or a name that fits two existing pages
70	  (or two entity types) with nothing in the source to settle it. Surface
71	  it as unresolved rather than guessing.
72	
73	## Notability gate
74	
75	Before treating an unmatched entity as a create candidate, apply the same
76	bar the CLI's internal DAG step uses: will you interact with this person again, or are
77	they relevant to your work or interests? Is the company relevant to work,
78	job search, or interests? Is the concept a reusable mental model worth
79	referencing again? A page clears the gate when it's likely to accumulate
80	history — a colleague the user will meet again, a company under evaluation,
81	a concept the source substantially develops. It doesn't clear the gate when
82	it's a drive-by mention — a name appearing once with no role in what
83	happened, a company named only as someone's past employer, a concept
84	mentioned but not developed.
85	
86	When in doubt, don't propose creation. A missing page can be created later
87	once the entity actually recurs; a junk page sits in every future search
88	result and degrades retrieval for everything else.
89	
90	## Holder ≠ subject
91	
92	When the source or note attributes a claim to someone, the entity you're
93	resolving as the claim's holder is whoever said or clearly implied it, not
94	whoever the claim is about. A founder describing their own company's
95	prospects is the holder — companies don't speak, their employees do. If
96	you're resolving "who is this claim attributed to" as part of matching, do
97	not resolve it to the company just because the company is the claim's
98	subject; resolve it to the person who made the statement, and let the
99	company be a separate entity if it's independently referenced.
100	
101	## Never auto-merge
102	
103	Do not resolve an ambiguous case by picking whichever candidate matched
104	first, and do not merge two existing pages into one because they look
105	similar. An entity that genuinely fits two existing pages, or fits none
106	cleanly, is more useful surfaced as ambiguous than silently collapsed into
107	a wrong match — a bad merge is harder to undo than an unresolved mention,
108	because it corrupts both pages' history. Preserve the ambiguity and let
109	`entity-enrichment` or the calling agent decide how to handle it (skip the
110	link, ask, or leave a flagged note).
111

1	---
2	name: entity-resolve
3	description: Judgment for deciding create/update/skip per entity a source touched.
4	skill_api: 1
5	---
6	
7	You are the entity-resolution step. The extraction step has already decided
8	what a source says; your different question is: for each person, company,
9	concept, project, or organization the source touched, does the knowledge
10	base already have a page for it, should one be created, or should the
11	mention be left alone?
12	
13	Decide one action per entity:
14	
15	- **update** — a page for this entity already exists among the existing
16	  notes provided. Point at its exact path. Leave proposed_frontmatter null —
17	  a later step decides what, if anything, on the page should change.
18	- **create** — no page exists, and the entity clears the notability bar:
19	  it is likely to accumulate history. A colleague the user will meet again,
20	  a company being evaluated, a concept the source substantially develops.
21	  Propose full frontmatter satisfying every required field of the entity's
22	  type, using only the types listed in the prompt.
23	- **skip** — a drive-by mention. A name that appears once with no role in
24	  what happened, a company named only as someone's past employer, a concept
25	  mentioned but not developed. Not every mentioned name deserves a page.
26	
27	Before proposing a create for a dated record type whose whole purpose is
28	logging what happened via this source (journal, meeting), check whether
29	this same source's content already has a home: is there an existing note —
30	of any type, not just one with a matching name — that already
31	substantively covers it, or that you're already resolving as action=update
32	in this same pass? A project's Timeline, a company's Compilation, whichever
33	accumulating page the source is really about can already capture the event
34	even though its own name never matches the dated record's title. Don't rely
35	on subject-name matching to catch this — a journal entry titled after its
36	own date and topic will essentially never share a name with the project or
37	company it's really about. If the source's content is already merged
38	somewhere else, that's a reason to skip the dated record, not a coincidence
39	to ignore.
40	
41	That same check runs the other way too, across proposals rather than
42	within one: when the source itself describes a dated occurrence — a
43	call, a meeting, an advisor or provider conversation — check the
44	existing notes provided for one that already covers that same date and
45	subject, not just an entity whose name matches a participant. An earlier
46	proposal may already have recorded this occurrence as a journal entry or
47	meeting note, even though nothing about it shares a name with the person
48	or company this source also touches. When one does, defer to it —
49	propose update against that existing note, or skip if it's already
50	fully captured — instead of creating a new entity of whatever type this
51	source would otherwise suggest. Confirmation rounds on this failure have
52	landed on a different wrong destination type each time (a meeting page,
53	then a project, then a person); that instability is itself the tell that
54	the miss is "never checked for an existing record of this occurrence,"
55	not "picked the wrong type once checking was done."
56	
57	Some sources are not really about one primary entity at all — they're
58	themselves an index or list spanning many (a reading tracker, a running
59	project list, a reflective entry that's really two separate dated
60	entries stitched together). Recognize that shape explicitly: resolve the
61	source itself as its own entry (`entity_type: index`, `action: create`)
62	alongside whatever entities it references, rather than only resolving
63	the entities it mentions and letting the source's own list-of-many
64	nature go unrecorded. An index that gets no resolution of its own
65	vanishes from the output with no visible trace that anything was
66	skipped.
67	
68	Resolving that index entity as `entity_type: index` is not automatic,
69	though — check first whether it even needs the cross-cutting MOC/
70	navigation type at all. A list confined to one category (a woodworking
71	project-list, a single project's own task index) is category content,
72	not vault-wide navigation, and belongs to that category's own type —
73	project, reference, whichever sibling notes filed under the same
74	directory already use — by the same category-context and sibling-
75	precedent signal the Rules section below applies to reference material.
76	`index` has `directory: null`: no canonical destination, a deliberate
77	design choice for genuine cross-category navigation, and a dead end for
78	anything else. Reserve it for a list that truly spans multiple
79	categories; don't let it become the default landing type for every
80	source that merely happens to be list-shaped.
81	
82	Notability gate — apply before every create, not after: a missing page
83	costs nothing (it can be created the next time the entity actually
84	matters); a junk page costs real attention and degrades search for
85	everyone later. **When in doubt about a drive-by mention, don't create —
86	skip instead.** That bias is for mentions, not for the source's own
87	subject: a source with real, attributable content about a single entity —
88	a single-URL bookmark, a short reference link, a sparse build-plan note —
89	clears the bar even when the content is thin. Create a minimal stub
90	rather than skip it; a stub can always be filled in later, but a skip
91	leaves no trace at all. That stub is never `entity_type: source` for the
92	source you're resolving right now — it's already captured as the raw file
93	being enriched, so proposing it again as its own entity just mirrors what
94	already exists rather than creating anything. Name the actual best-fit
95	domain type for the subject (project, concept, person, whatever the
96	content is really about) and create that instead.
97	
98	- Person: will the user plausibly interact with them again, or are they
99	  otherwise relevant to ongoing work? A name surfaced once with no
100	  continuing role does not clear this bar on its own.
101	- Company: relevant to the user's work, interests, or an active
102	  evaluation (a job search, a vendor decision, a deal)?
103	- Concept/project/other: an actual reusable idea or body of work, not a
104	  passing reference.
105	- Identity uncertainty is its own reason to skip: if a name looks like it
106	  could be a mishearing or transcription error (one odd, uncorroborated
107	  mention, especially where the role it's attached to — "the CEO," "my
108	  manager" — is already known some other way), don't invent a low-
109	  confidence page for a possibly-wrong name. A skipped mention is
110	  reviewable later; a wrong page fragments the entity it should have
111	  pointed at.
112	
113	Rules:
114	
115	- Use only the entity types listed in the prompt, exactly as spelled. If an
116	  entity fits none of them, skip it — the pipeline hard-stops on unknown
117	  types rather than guessing a schema.
118	- One source routinely touches several entities (a meeting touches people,
119	  a company, and a project at once). Resolve each independently; do not
120	  collapse them into one destination.
121	- When an entity genuinely fits two types and nothing in the source settles
122	  it, skip it rather than picking whichever matched first — an ambiguous
123	  case surfaced to the user beats a silently wrong page.
124	- Category context and sibling-note precedent often do settle it, though,
125	  before you reach for skip. Reference material — a bare excerpt, a
126	  third-party instructional piece — that lives within a specific
127	  craft/project category, with no personal reading record attached, belongs
128	  to that category's own reference type, not the general reading-category
129	  type it superficially resembles. Check whether sibling notes already
130	  filed under the same source directory or category were resolved a
131	  particular way; existing precedent there is a strong signal, and matching
132	  it beats re-deriving the type from content shape alone.
133	- Before precedent can even apply, settle whose work the source is
134	  describing — voice and perspective decide that, not how much build detail
135	  is on the page. A source written in the third person about a build the
136	  user is not personally executing — a blog post, an instructional article,
137	  "the author built...", someone else's "I made this, here's how" — is
138	  reference material describing someone else's work, however much
139	  hands-on construction detail it contains. A personal build log is the
140	  user's own account, in their own first-person voice, of their own
141	  in-progress work. Don't let build-log-shaped content (steps, materials,
142	  photos) stand in for this judgment; a detailed how-to about someone
143	  else's project is still reference material, not the user's project.
144	- Match against existing notes by identity, not string equality: "Jane",
145	  "Jane Doe", and "jane-doe" are the same person if the context says so. Do
146	  not create a duplicate page for a spelling variant of an existing note.
147	- Names in proposed frontmatter carry the authored, human casing — never
148	  slugs.
149	- The same identity check applies across word forms, not just spelling: a
150	  candidate concept that is really just the abstract-noun or adjective form
151	  of a subject this proposal already treats as primary — the concept a book
152	  is about, when that book is this source's own proposed_note or an entity
153	  it's also updating — is one idea wearing two names, not two entities.
154	  Skip the redundant create; the primary entity's own content is where that
155	  idea belongs. This is a judgment call about what the source is actually
156	  about, not a spelling or substring match — two entities that merely share
157	  a word root (two similarly-named companies, say) are still two entities,
158	  and nothing here licenses skipping either of them.
159	
160	## Relevance: how much does the source actually concern this entity?
161	
162	Separate from confidence (below), every entity you resolve also gets a
163	`relevance` judgment: how much *this particular source* concerns them —
164	not how important they are in general, and not how easy they were to
165	resolve. This matters most for action=update: it decides whether the
166	entity's page is worth the cost of a full revision pass later, so judge
167	it from what the source actually does with the entity.
168	
169	- **central** — a primary subject of the source, or a participant in it.
170	- **notable** — a real stakeholder in what's discussed, even if they're
171	  not personally discussed at length (e.g. one of several people a
172	  decision affects, named but never individually talked about).
173	- **minor** — mentioned with some context, but not a focus of the source.
174	- **peripheral** — named only as background. The source isn't really
175	  about them, even if the mention is substantively true.
176	
177	Worked example, from a planning call between two participants scoping a
178	consulting engagement: the two participants and the project being scoped
179	are **central**. Colleagues named as affected by the outcome but never
180	personally discussed are **notable**. A colleague named in passing with a
181	caveat ("short tenure, no read on him yet") is **minor**. A company named
182	only as *"the reason I only have two weeks free"* is **peripheral** — it
183	explains a constraint the other side cares about, but the source isn't
184	about that company. Conflating "this explains something important" with
185	"this entity is relevant" is the mistake to avoid.
186	
187	## Confidence: is this the right page?
188	
189	`confidence` is a different question — identity-match certainty, not
190	relevance. A distinctly-named, unambiguous entity resolves with high
191	confidence even when it's barely mentioned (peripheral + high confidence
192	is a normal combination, not a contradiction); a common or ambiguous name
193	gets lower confidence even when it's central to the source.
194	
195	## Whose content is this: first-person reflection vs. what it references
196	
197	A source written in the first person — the author's own reaction,
198	opinion, or reflection, as opposed to a factual record, a build log, or
199	reference material — is about its author. Resolve that reflective content
200	as its own journal entry (or whichever dated-record type fits) regardless
201	of how many other works, articles, or projects it discusses along the
202	way. Don't let the entities merely referenced substitute for capturing
203	the reflection itself: an article stub or a book stub, created and left
204	empty, is not a replacement for the first-person entry that should have
205	been proposed alongside them. This is both/and, not either/or — resolve
206	the source's own reflective content as journal, and separately resolve
207	each referenced work as an ordinary entity mention subject to the
208	notability gate above. The bug this guards against is the reflection
209	being dropped entirely in favor of only the secondary references, not
210	the references being resolved at all.
211

1	---
2	name: entity-enrichment
3	description: Decide which existing entities a note should link to, propose creating entities that clear the notability gate, and add texture — beliefs, motivations, trajectory — rather than a bare fact sheet. Use after entity-resolution has matched a note's mentions, whenever you're deciding how a note connects to the knowledge base.
4	skill_api: 1
5	---
6	
7	# entity-enrichment
8	
9	`entity-resolution` answers "does this mention correspond to an existing
10	page, and does it warrant one?" This skill picks up from there and answers
11	the next question: **given those resolution results, how should the note
12	actually connect?**
13	
14	```text
15	entity-resolution → determine what an entity refers to
16	entity-enrichment → decide how the note should connect to it
17	```
18	
19	If you're checking whether "Jane" is `people/jane-doe.md`, that's
20	`entity-resolution`. If you're deciding whether this mention of Jane earns a
21	back-link, whether her page's State (Compiled Truth) needs updating, or
22	whether a brand-new page for her is worth creating at all — that's here.
23	Never skip straight to linking or creating without resolving identity
24	first; this skill consumes `entity-resolution`'s output, it doesn't
25	re-derive it.
26	
27	## When to use
28	
29	- Whenever a note or source references a person, company, project, or
30	  concept and `entity-resolution` has already produced a match, a create
31	  candidate, or an ambiguous result for it — during `ingest-source`,
32	  `note-revision`, or any manual edit that touches entity mentions.
33	- Anywhere you're about to add a `[[wikilink]]`, fill in a page's texture
34	  sections, or propose a new entity page and need to decide whether it's
35	  worth doing.
36	
37	## Where wakil's own pipeline stops — and why this skill exists
38	
39	`wakil enrich <source-id>` already runs entity resolution and, for every
40	`action: create` result, writes a schema-valid stub
41	(`_build_stub_entities`, `src/wakil/app/ingest_service.py`): frontmatter
42	carrying only what the CLI's internal resolution DAG step proposed plus
43	`created`/`updated`, and a body skeleton of `## Compiled Truth`,
44	`## Open Threads`, and `## Timeline / Log` (`_stub_content`). A follow-up
45	model call in the same DAG pass (`_synthesize_stub_content`, issue #70)
46	then tries to replace that skeleton with a first Compiled Truth and
47	Timeline entry grounded in *this one source* — reusing the exact
48	`EntityRevision`/note-revision machinery `_run_entity_updates` uses for
49	existing notes, since a from-scratch stub and a still-unpopulated one
50	(`_is_unpopulated_stub`) are the same problem. When the source genuinely
51	doesn't support real content for that entity, or the synthesis call itself
52	fails, the plain placeholder is left in place — never a fabrication — with
53	a visible warning in the enrich preview.
54	
55	That's still identity resolution and single-source scaffolding, not full
56	enrichment. The CLI path does not decide which of the source's *other*
57	mentions deserve a back-link, does not draw on any *other* existing
58	knowledge about the entity (no cross-referencing `related_notes`, no
59	research beyond this one source), and does not add Timeline entries beyond
60	what this one source supports.
61	
62	That broader judgment — cross-referencing what the knowledge base already
63	knows, deciding which other mentions earn a link, building out texture
64	beyond what a single source can support — is this skill's job. Applied to
65	a freshly-stubbed page (whether or not the CLI's own pass already
66	populated it), an existing page being updated with new signal, or a
67	mention encountered during `note-revision` or manual editing, anywhere
68	outside the CLI's fixed DAG.
69	
70	## Procedure
71	
72	For each entity `entity-resolution` returned for the note in hand:
73	
74	1. **Confident match.** Decide whether this specific mention earns a
75	   back-link (see "Avoid superficial linking" below), and whether the
76	   mention carries signal material enough to update the matched page's
77	   Compiled Truth or add a Timeline entry. Not every match needs a page
78	   edit — a passing reference that adds no new fact just gets the link.
79	2. **Create candidate (cleared the notability gate).** Hand the page to
80	   `note-routing` for its destination directory and filename (entity
81	   directories come from `schema.directory` — `people/` for `person`,
82	   `companies/` for `company` — never invent one), then write real content:
83	   Compiled Truth with texture, not `[No data yet]` boilerplate, plus a
84	   first Timeline entry. `note-conformance` is the pass that checks the
85	   result is schema-valid before it's committed — this skill decides
86	   content, not shape.
87	3. **No match, not notable, or ambiguous.** Don't force a link and don't
88	   create a page. See "Preserve ambiguity" below.
89	
90	## Scale effort to importance
91	
92	Not every entity deserves the same investment. Before writing anything,
93	weigh how much this entity matters to the user's ongoing work: a close,
94	recurring contact or a company under active evaluation earns a thorough
95	pass — real research into what's changed, a full texture rewrite if
96	material. A name that surfaces once with light but genuine relevance earns
97	a light pass — a Timeline entry and a link, nothing more. Don't spend the
98	same effort tracking down background on someone who appears once in passing
99	as you would on someone the user works with weekly; effort is a dial, not a
100	fixed procedure.
101	
102	## Texture over facts
103	
104	A page's Compiled Truth should read like an intelligence dossier, not a
105	scraped fact sheet. Hard facts (role, company, status) are table stakes —
106	what makes a page worth having is texture: what does this person believe,
107	what are they building, what's driving them, where is their trajectory
108	headed. When updating an existing page, re-synthesize Compiled Truth to
109	cover the union of what was already known plus the new signal — never
110	replace it with only what the newest source said, and treat "my rewritten
111	section is shorter than what was there" as a stop-and-check signal, not
112	confirmation you're done. Timeline entries are append-only: add dated
113	entries, never delete or reorder what's already there, including
114	auto-generated back-link lines.
115	
116	## Send existing knowledge as context, not a rehash
117	
118	Before writing new content into a page, check what the knowledge base
119	already knows about the entity — this is exactly what `prepare_enrichment`
120	already does for you in the CLI path (`search_workspace` builds
121	`related_notes`, threaded into both the extraction and resolution prompts
122	so the model reasons from what's already known rather than from nothing).
123	When working by hand outside that path, do the same thing manually: search
124	for the entity's existing page and related mentions first, then let the new
125	source contribute only the delta — what's new or what contradicts prior
126	Compiled Truth — instead of re-deriving the whole page from the one source
127	in front of you.
128	
129	## Mandatory author-page creation
130	
131	Anyone whose thinking is worth ingesting is worth tracking. When a note
132	captures someone's original thinking — an article, an essay, a tweet, a
133	standalone idea — the author gets a page if `entity-resolution` doesn't
134	already find one, regardless of how minor their other mentions in the piece
135	would otherwise read. This is a standing exception to the general
136	notability gate, not a bypass of resolution: still resolve the author's
137	identity first to check for an existing page, but the act of ingesting
138	their original thinking is itself the notability signal — a person whose
139	thinking justified capturing an entire note is not a drive-by mention.
140	
141	## Avoid superficial or excessive linking
142	
143	A back-link earns its place when the mention is substantive — the note says
144	something about the entity, not just that the entity was in the room. Don't
145	wikilink every incidental name-drop; a page whose every sentence is
146	studded with links is harder to read, not more connected. When a matched
147	entity has its own page, still create the back-link from that entity's page
148	to this one — an unlinked substantive mention is a broken connection — but
149	apply the same judgment in both directions: link what matters, skip what's
150	incidental.
151	
152	That "is it substantive enough" judgment call is for matches
153	`entity-resolution` surfaced by search. A related note the user pointed at
154	explicitly — reached through an `@file:` reference in the source's context,
155	not just found by `search_workspace` — carries a different signal: the user
156	picked that note deliberately, so treat it as high-confidence and back-link
157	it rather than weighing the mention against the substantive bar above.
158	
159	That confidence is about the link decision only — it says nothing about
160	content-worthiness. Whether the mention also earns a Compiled Truth edit or
161	a Timeline entry is still governed by the ordinary test in "Confident
162	match" above: does it carry a new fact, development, or contradiction? An
163	explicit `@file:` reference to a page that's mentioned only in passing —
164	nothing new said about it — still gets just the link, exactly as any other
165	passing reference would.
166	
167	## Preserve ambiguity
168	
169	Don't resolve an ambiguous or no-match case by picking the closest-looking
170	candidate, forcing a link anyway, or merging it into an existing page that's
171	only a rough fit. This is the same discipline `entity-resolution` applies at
172	the identity layer — carry it forward here: an unresolved mention left
173	unlinked is recoverable later; a wrong link or a bad merge corrupts two
174	pages' history and is far harder to undo. When in doubt, leave the mention
175	unlinked and say so rather than guessing.
176	
177	## Where the output goes next
178	
179	This skill decides content — which links, which pages, what goes in
180	Compiled Truth and Timeline. It does not decide destination directories or
181	filenames (`note-routing`'s job) and does not do the final schema/prose
182	audit (`note-conformance`'s job, including the `name:`/`title:` category
183	rule and slug consistency). Hand off to both before anything gets
184	committed.
185

1	---
2	name: entity-compile
3	description: Re-synthesize an entity's Compiled Truth as the union of every fact already present in its own Timeline — no new source involved. Use for `wakil entities compile SLUG` only, never as a substitute for note-revision's ordinary merge.
4	skill_api: 1
5	---
6	
7	# entity-compile
8	
9	`note-revision/SKILL.md` already defines the State/Timeline discipline this
10	skill runs on: Compiled Truth is *re-synthesized* on every update to cover
11	the union of what was already there plus what's new, and Timeline is
12	*append-only*, never touched by a synthesis step. This skill doesn't restate
13	that discipline — read it there. What's different here is narrower: there is
14	no new source. "What's new" is empty. The entire input is one entity's own
15	existing Timeline, and the job is to produce a Compiled Truth that actually
16	reflects it, for notes where synthesis never ran (docs/adr/0016's audit
17	finding: Compiled Truth empty or placeholder for most of the vault, with the
18	real content sitting unsynthesized in Timeline).
19	
20	**Why a separate skill file, not `note-revision` directly:** ADR 0016 asks
21	for reuse to be tried first, and only split out "if reuse proves genuinely
22	awkward in practice." It is, here, concretely: `note-revision`'s procedure
23	(Step 2 "re-read the raw source for the new facts," Step 3 "classify the new
24	material... additive, contradicting, or duplicate," the three-tier dedup
25	heuristic, and "Resolving conflicting sources" across multiple sources) is
26	built entirely around comparing new material to what's already on the page.
27	Compile has no new material to classify — every fact is already on the page,
28	by definition. Pointing a model at that procedure with nothing to classify
29	would be confusing, not merely redundant, so the exception case ADR 0016
30	itself names applies. What does transfer directly, and is the actual
31	foundation this skill stands on, is the State/Timeline discipline above —
32	that part is cited, not restated.
33	
34	## What this does
35	
36	Read the given Timeline in full. Write a Compiled Truth paragraph (or a few)
37	that is the union of every fact it contains — not a diff, not a rewrite from
38	memory of the entity, a synthesis grounded only in the Timeline text given.
39	
40	## Hard constraint: additive only
41	
42	This is not a compression or summarization task. Every fact already present
43	in the Timeline must be present, in some form, in the Compiled Truth you
44	write. Worst case, the result is verbose or a little redundant — that's a
45	safe failure. Dropping a still-true fact is not; it's the same clobbering
46	failure note-revision's three-tier dedup heuristic and clobbering-bug
47	warning both exist to prevent, applied here to a case where there's no new
48	source to classify a fact against — only the question of whether two
49	Timeline entries are the same fact restated or two distinct ones.
50	
51	**When in doubt, don't silently resolve it: include both.** If two entries
52	look like they might describe the same underlying fact (same subject,
53	close-but-not-identical dates or figures) but you're not certain, keep both
54	in the output rather than merging them into one or guessing which is stale.
55	A reader can tolerate two similar sentences; they can't recover a fact that
56	silently vanished.
57	
58	## Pronouns and invented detail
59	
60	Two constraints that apply to every sentence you write about a person:
61	
62	- **Carry forward whatever pronouns are already there; never introduce one.**
63	  If the Timeline and the existing top section use "she", keep using "she" —
64	  that is established content, and changing it is a factual claim, not a
65	  compression. If they use no gendered pronoun, don't add one: use they/them
66	  or restructure around the person's name. Never infer from a first name, a
67	  role, or context.
68	
69	  Deliberately phrased against the entries rather than against a `pronouns:`
70	  frontmatter field, because this call never sees frontmatter — `prepare_entity_compile`
71	  hands you `post.content` only. A rule keyed on a field you can't read would
72	  resolve to "no field, use they/them" every time, rewriting correct prose on
73	  a page that does declare pronouns. `note-revision`, which does see
74	  frontmatter, is the stage that records and honours the field.
75	- **Never add specifics the Timeline doesn't contain.** Compiling means
76	  restating what the entries already say more readably. A number, a date, or
77	  a quote that isn't in the source entries is not a compression of them.
78	
79	## What this does NOT do
80	
81	- **No lossy "collapse stale detail" compression.** Deciding what's safe to
82	  drop as outdated is a different, harder judgment with no calibration data
83	  behind it yet — explicitly out of scope for this skill version (ADR 0016).
84	  If an old Timeline entry is superseded by a newer one, say so in the
85	  synthesis (e.g. "originally X, later revised to Y") rather than silently
86	  omitting the earlier value.
87	- **Never proposes a Timeline entry.** Timeline is passed through to the
88	  caller untouched — not edited, reordered, or appended to. That's a
89	  property of how this skill is invoked (the caller never asks for a
90	  Timeline edit here), worth stating plainly anyway so a reader doesn't
91	  assume this is a general-purpose revision pass.
92	- **Not a substitute for note-revision.** A source with genuinely new
93	  information about an entity still goes through note-revision's ordinary
94	  merge; this skill only runs when the "new" material is nothing at all —
95	  just the entity's own accumulated history, unsynthesized.
96	
97	## Worked example
98	
99	`companies/mosaic-private-markets.md` is exactly the shape this skill exists
100	for: a large Timeline of dated interview and meeting notes, an empty or
101	placeholder Compiled Truth. Its Timeline might contain entries like:
102	
103	```text
104	### 2026-05-02 — intro call
105	- Mosaic is raising a $40M Series B, targeting a Q3 close.
106	- Lead investor not yet confirmed.
107	
108	### 2026-05-20 — follow-up with CFO
109	- Series B target confirmed at $40M; CFO says they're now in
110	  term-sheet discussions with two lead candidates.
111	- Use of proceeds: 60% platform engineering, 40% go-to-market.
112	
113	### 2026-06-14 — partner meeting
114	- One of the two lead candidates dropped out over valuation.
115	- Remaining lead (unnamed) has verbally agreed to term sheet;
116	  signing expected early Q3.
117	```
118	
119	These are related but not redundant: the raise size is confirmed across all
120	three, the lead-investor status changes entry to entry, and the
121	use-of-proceeds detail appears only once. A correct Compiled Truth keeps all
122	of it, distinctly:
123	
124	> Mosaic is raising a $40M Series B (target confirmed as of 2026-05-20),
125	> planned for a Q3 close, allocating proceeds roughly 60% to platform
126	> engineering and 40% go-to-market. Two lead-investor candidates were in
127	> term-sheet discussions as of 2026-05-20; one dropped out over valuation by
128	> 2026-06-14, leaving one remaining candidate who has verbally agreed to
129	> terms with signing expected early Q3.
130	
131	Note what this is *not*: it doesn't drop the use-of-proceeds split just
132	because it appeared in only one entry, and it doesn't silently pick "one
133	lead investor" as the final state without naming that the field narrowed
134	from two candidates to one over time — both entries' facts survive, in
135	synthesized form, even though the raw Timeline entries themselves are left
136	exactly as they were.
137	
138	## Full resynthesis mode
139	
140	Everything above is this skill's default, additive-only judgment, used for
141	the ordinary `wakil entities compile SLUG` call. `wakil entities compile
142	SLUG --full` (docs/adr/0017, Stage 2) invokes this same skill for a second,
143	deliberately different judgment: **full resynthesis**, the one place this
144	skill is allowed to drop content. This section states exactly where that
145	permission ends; "Hard constraint: additive only" above still governs every
146	other invocation, including this one's own treatment of Timeline itself —
147	full resynthesis never touches, reorders, or proposes an edit to Timeline
148	any more than additive mode does. It also never sees the note's *current*
149	Compiled Truth — that omission is a property of the prompt you're given
150	(docs/adr/0017), not a judgment call to make: every full resynthesis is a
151	fresh re-derivation from Timeline alone, never an edit of a prior run's
152	output.
153	
154	**Your output is the synthesized Compiled Truth prose, and nothing else.**
155	Do not explain, inside your output, what you added, dropped, or why — no
156	"What was dropped, and why" section, no aside naming a superseded value
157	you removed, no meta-commentary about the compression itself. Whatever you
158	return becomes the note's actual Compiled Truth section verbatim; any
159	explanation of your reasoning bloats exactly the thing this operation
160	exists to keep small, and a dropped value named in an "originally X, now
161	Y" aside is still present in the output, which the redundancy rule above
162	already forbids once a fact is judged clearly superseded. The worked
163	example below labels its "what was dropped and why" commentary
164	separately, after the example output, precisely because that commentary
165	is for a human reading this skill file — it documents the *reasoning*
166	behind the example, it is not part of the *result* the example shows.
167	
168	### The two-part salience rule
169	
170	Two independent judgments decide what full resynthesis may compress or
171	drop. Apply both; neither alone is the right rule — a frequency-only
172	reading ("keep only what's repeated" or, just as wrong the other way,
173	"protect anything stated only once") would license removing almost
174	nothing, since most of a bloated Compiled Truth is likely distinct,
175	once-stated content, not redundant restatement.
176	
177	1. **Redundancy (frequency-based).** The same underlying fact, restated or
178	   updated across multiple Timeline entries, collapses toward its current
179	   value. This is the one real behavioral difference from additive mode's
180	   dedup above: where a later entry clearly and unambiguously supersedes
181	   an earlier one — not a fuzzy, uncertain match — the earlier restatement
182	   may be dropped entirely, not merely condensed or kept alongside a
183	   "originally X, later Y" note. If the two entries aren't clearly the
184	   same fact narrowing to one value, this rule doesn't apply — fall back
185	   to "when in doubt, include both," the same as additive mode.
186	2. **Durability (a fact stated exactly once).** A fact mentioned only once
187	   isn't redundant with anything, so rule 1 never reaches it. The question
188	   instead is whether it's *durable* — an identifying detail, a decision,
189	   a commitment, an ongoing status or relationship fact, the kind of thing
190	   `note-revision`'s own State discipline treats as belonging in Compiled
191	   Truth permanently — or *ephemeral* — a scheduling detail, a
192	   meeting-day operational note whose relevance was spent the day it
193	   happened. Durable once-stated facts are never eligible for removal,
194	   full stop, regardless of how far over target the note runs. Ephemeral
195	   once-stated facts may be compressed or dropped, but only once whatever
196	   durable consequence they led to is already captured elsewhere in your
197	   output — a since-superseded "let's meet at 3pm" is droppable once the
198	   note already reflects that the meeting happened and what came of it,
199	   not before.
200	
201	**When genuinely uncertain whether a once-stated fact is durable or
202	ephemeral, default to durable.** This mirrors the "when in doubt, include
203	both" bias above, applied to a different ambiguity, because the cost here
204	is asymmetric too: wrongly calling a fact durable costs a little extra
205	verbosity in an operation that exists to save space; wrongly calling it
206	ephemeral silently deletes something true. When size pressure and
207	uncertainty pull in opposite directions, uncertainty wins.
208	
209	### Worked example
210	
211	`people/carla-nunez.md`'s Timeline has grown long enough that its Compiled
212	Truth is well over target. Relevant entries:
213	
214	```text
215	### 2026-03-04 -- first intro
216	- Carla is the VP of Underwriting at Northfield Mutual.
217	- She mentioned the team is piloting a new risk-scoring model, no
218	  timeline given yet.
219	
220	### 2026-03-18 -- pilot kickoff
221	- Risk-scoring pilot timeline confirmed: targeting a Q3 go-live, 90-day
222	  evaluation window against the current model.
223	- Meeting moved from Tuesday to Thursday this week because Carla was
224	  traveling -- rescheduled for 2026-03-19 at 2pm.
225	
226	### 2026-03-19 -- rescheduled check-in
227	- Confirmed pilot is on track; no material change to the Q3 go-live
228	  target discussed on 2026-03-18.
229	- Carla's team lead on the pilot is Priya Shah.
230	```
231	
232	Two things a correct full resynthesis does here that additive mode above
233	would not:
234	
235	- **Redundancy, resolved by dropping.** The pilot timeline is mentioned
236	  three times: "no timeline given yet" (2026-03-04), "Q3 go-live, 90-day
237	  window" (2026-03-18), and "on track, no material change" (2026-03-19).
238	  These clearly narrow to one current value. Full resynthesis states only
239	  the current one — a Q3 go-live pilot, on track as of the latest
240	  check-in — and drops the superseded "no timeline given yet" entirely,
241	  not condensed alongside it. Additive mode would have kept all three;
242	  this is the one real behavioral difference between the two modes.
243	- **Ephemeral fact, compressed away.** The Tuesday-to-Thursday reschedule
244	  is a once-stated, scheduling-only fact. Its only durable consequence —
245	  that the 2026-03-19 check-in happened and confirmed the pilot on track —
246	  is already captured. The reschedule reason and original day are
247	  dropped; nothing about it was durable in its own right.
248	
249	What survives intact, and must: Carla's title (VP of Underwriting,
250	Northfield Mutual) and Priya Shah as the pilot's team lead — both durable,
251	once-stated identifying/relationship facts, neither eligible for
252	compression under any size pressure.
253	
254	**Your entire output would be** — nothing before or after this, no
255	heading, no explanation:
256	
257	> Carla Nunez is VP of Underwriting at Northfield Mutual. Her team is
258	> running a risk-scoring model pilot, on track for a Q3 go-live against a
259	> 90-day evaluation window as of the 2026-03-19 check-in; Priya Shah leads
260	> the pilot on Carla's team.
261	
262	*(For this documentation's benefit, not part of the output above — a
263	reader of this skill file, not the model producing an output, is the
264	audience for the rest of this paragraph.)* What it dropped, and why: the
265	original "no timeline given yet" framing
266	(superseded by the confirmed Q3 target — redundancy rule) and the
267	Tuesday-to-Thursday reschedule detail (ephemeral, its consequence already
268	folded into "as of the 2026-03-19 check-in" — durability rule). Everything
269	else — the title, the pilot's existence, the Q3 target, the 90-day window,
270	Priya's role — is durable, or the current value of a redundant chain, and
271	stays.
272	
273	### A note on `eval.json`'s repeat-run scenario
274	
275	The repeat-run scenario in this skill's `eval.json` (eval scenario d) is a
276	best-effort approximation of ADR 0017's anti-compounding requirement, not
277	a literal test of it. `tests/evals/runner.py` makes exactly one model call
278	per scenario, so it can't actually invoke full resynthesis twice in
279	sequence and compare the two outputs the way the requirement describes.
280	The scenario instead asks the model to treat a fabricated "prior run's"
281	Compiled Truth as something to check its own answer against afterward,
282	not read from — which the model isn't structurally prevented from ignoring
283	the way the real code path is. **The real guarantee is structural, not
284	behavioral**: `build_full_resynthesis_prompt` never includes the note's
285	current Compiled Truth at all, verified directly against actual call
286	arguments in
287	`tests/unit/test_ingest_service.py::test_prepare_entity_full_resynthesis_happy_path_and_timeline_only_prompt`.
288	That unit test, not this eval scenario, is the real evidence for the
289	no-compounding claim; treat the eval scenario as a supplementary sanity
290	check on output quality, not the proof.

"""Load judgment content from SKILL.md and build system prompts.

Skill files carry prose only — heuristics, anti-patterns, worked examples.
The JSON shape the model must return is never written into a skill file; it
is generated here from the Pydantic contract's `model_json_schema()`, so the
schema the model sees and the schema `validate_model_response` checks are
always the same object (docs/ingestion-refactor-spec.md).

Skill content is resolved through `wakil.skills.resolver` — the same
precedence chain `wakil skills list/which/validate/lint` use
(`WAKIL_SKILL_PATH` -> `<kb-root>/skills` -> user-level -> built-in). A
knowledge base can override `article`/`text`/`transcript`/`entity-resolve`
just like any other catalog skill, and that override actually takes effect
here — this is the one place their content gets read for `wakil enrich`.
"""

Read all four SKILL.md files and traced how each is wired in code. Here's the comparison.

## They split on two axes, not one

**Axis 1 — who reads the skill:**

| Skill | Consumer | Wiring |
|---|---|---|
| `entity-resolve` | a model call inside the `enrich` DAG | `load_skill("entity-resolve")` — `ingest_service.py:1706` |
| `entity-compile` | a model call inside `wakil entities compile` | `load_skill("entity-compile")` — `ingest_service.py:3392` (additive) and `:3458` (`--full`) |
| `entity-resolution` | an outer agent editing by hand | prompt-only; no code loads it |
| `entity-enrichment` | an outer agent editing by hand | prompt-only (`schema_validate_service.py:5`) |

**Axis 2 — which question they answer**, in pipeline order:

```
what is this entity?  →  how should the note connect?  →  what does the page now say?
  resolve/resolution         enrichment                       compile
```

## The pairs

**`entity-resolve` ⟷ `entity-resolution` are the same judgment, deliberately duplicated across execution contexts.** `entity-resolve` is the system prompt for the always-invoked second model call in `wakil enrich`; it emits a machine-consumed `create`/`update`/`skip` per entity plus `relevance` and `confidence` fields, and proposes full frontmatter for creates (because `_build_stub_entities` downstream turns that into a schema-routed stub page). `entity-resolution` is the hand-editing counterpart — it opens by telling you *not* to run it if you're going through the CLI ("The CLI path already does this — don't duplicate it"), and it exists so a note edited during `note-revision` and a note produced by `enrich` don't disagree about whether "Jane" is `people/jane-doe.md`. It stops at three outcomes (match / create candidate / ambiguous) and explicitly refuses to create the page itself, handing that to `entity-enrichment`.

**`entity-resolution` ⟷ `entity-enrichment` are a clean handoff at the identity/connection seam**, and both state the boundary in the same two-line diagram: resolution determines *what an entity refers to*, enrichment decides *how the note should connect to it*. Enrichment's most useful section is its map of where the CLI stops: `_build_stub_entities` + `_synthesize_stub_content` scaffold a stub from *this one source only* — no cross-referencing `related_notes`, no back-links to the source's other mentions, no Timeline beyond what one source supports. That residue is precisely enrichment's job.

**`entity-compile` is the cleanup pass for debt the other three create.** Resolve mints stubs; enrichment and `note-revision` append to Timeline; Compiled Truth drifts or never gets written at all — ADR 0016's audit found it empty or placeholder across most of the vault with the real content sitting unsynthesized in Timeline. Compile is the only one of the four that takes **no new source**: its entire input is the entity's own Timeline. It documents why it isn't just `note-revision` (that skill's whole procedure is built on classifying *new* material as additive/contradicting/duplicate, and compile has no new material to classify).

## What makes them compose rather than overlap

They share a doctrine, enforced in four places:

- **Notability gate** — "when in doubt, don't create; a missing page costs nothing, a junk page degrades every future search" (resolve + resolution, near-verbatim).
- **Never auto-merge / preserve ambiguity** — an unresolved mention is recoverable, a bad merge corrupts two pages' history (resolution + enrichment, which explicitly says it's carrying resolution's discipline forward).
- **Additive bias** — enrichment: re-synthesize Compiled Truth as the union, and treat "my rewrite is shorter" as a stop-and-check signal. Compile: "when in doubt, include both."
- **State vs. Timeline** — Compiled Truth re-synthesized, Timeline append-only. Both enrichment and compile cite `note-revision` for it rather than restating it.

And each one terminates rather than overreaching: resolution → enrichment → `note-routing` (destination) → `note-conformance` (schema/prose audit).

## Three tensions worth knowing about

1. **`entity-compile --full` is the single licensed exception to the additive doctrine** the other three enforce. Its two-part salience rule (redundancy: a clearly superseded fact may be *dropped*, not condensed; durability: a once-stated fact is droppable only if ephemeral, and uncertainty defaults to durable) is the whole guardrail keeping that carve-out from becoming general permission to compress.

2. **`entity-resolve` has grown well past `entity-resolution`.** It carries a lot of bug-driven guidance the hand-editing twin never picked up: the dated-record dedup check (both directions — within a pass and across proposals), the `index` entity-type trap, "first-person reflection is both/and, not either/or," identity-uncertainty-as-skip, the reference-vs-personal-build-log voice test. `entity-resolution` claims to encode "the same judgment the CLI's internal DAG step encodes" — true for the notability gate and identity matching, but the claim is drifting. If you hand-edit outside `enrich`, you're running an older version of that judgment.

3. **The names are genuinely confusable**, and the repo knows it — `skill-authoring/SKILL.md:206` warns against citing `entity-resolve` as if it were an outer-agent skill. `entity-resolve`/`entity-compile` are DAG-internal system prompts; `entity-resolution`/`entity-enrichment` are agent guidance. Nothing in the names tells you that.

No files changed — this was read-only analysis; I checked each skill's wiring in `ingest_service.py` and `skill_loader.py` rather than inferring from the prose.

They share a notability/never-merge/additive doctrine; the notable tensions are `--full` resynthesis as the one licensed exception to additive-only, and `entity-resolution` having drifted behind `entity-resolve`'s accumulated guidance.

## PR review — `pr-reviewer`

### Verification run (on the PR head)

```
uv run pytest -q -m "not eval"   →  787 passed, 68 deselected in 72.39s
uv run ruff check .              →  All checks passed!
uvx ty check .                   →  All checks passed!
uv run pytest -m eval --collect-only | grep transcript
   → transcript-mixed-material-one-transcript
   → transcript-decision-reversal-anchors-on-where-it-landed
```

The PR's `787 passed`, ruff-clean and ty-clean claims all hold, and both new scenarios collect and validate against `EvalScenario`. No live eval was run — no point re-spending model budget on what the PR already sampled six times.

Two findings are bucket `fix`. Both are in the entity-resolve half, not the transcript half — the transcript work is measured and lands well.

| # | Finding | Bucket |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `EntityResolution.relevance`'s Field description still defines `notable`/`minor` by *focus*, the exact test the rewritten SKILL.md replaces — and both ship in the same system prompt | `fix` |
| 2 | `entity-resolve/SKILL.md` rewritten 210→287 lines in an undescribed second commit, with no `eval.json`; ADR 0015 gates this exact guidance on a live eval that still doesn't exist | `fix` |
| 3 | Commit 2 deletes the concrete `_LOW_RELEVANCE` consequence sentence the PR body names as the entity-resolve deliverable | `issue` |
| 4 | New `skip` wording licenses dropping precisely the third-party observation the transcript half exists to capture | `issue` |
| 5 | Transcript skill claims entity-resolution "can carry it to that person's own page", but memories are not an input to that call | `issue` |
| 6 | Pronoun rule asserts "You are not shown anyone's existing page" — true in production, false in the eval harness that grades it | `issue` |
| 7 | Worked example narrows `notable` in a way the level definition above it doesn't | `nit` |
| 8 | `relevance` now defined twice, in two sections separated by `## Rules` | `nit` |
| 9 | "When in doubt … skip instead" lost its bold emphasis | `nit` |
| 10 | `README.md:337` "Notable new entities (action `create`)" now contradicts the skill's notable≠create rule | `nit` |

---

### Fix 1 — the schema field description contradicts the skill prose, in the same prompt

`src/wakil/llm/schemas.py:132-140` is unchanged by this PR:

```python
relevance: Literal["central", "notable", "minor", "peripheral"] | None = Field(
    default=None,
    description="How much this source actually concerns this entity — "
    "independent of confidence. central: a primary subject of or participant in "
    "the source. notable: a real stakeholder in what's discussed, even if not "
    "personally discussed at length. minor: mentioned with some context but not "
    "a focus. peripheral: named only as background — the source isn't really "
    "about them. See the skill body for worked examples.",
)
```

The PR's whole thesis for entity-resolve is `SKILL.md:169` — **"Length of mention is not the test; substance is."** — and `:161-163`, redefining `minor` as *"does not provide substantive information worth carrying into the entity's durable page."*

The schema says `minor` = "not a focus". The skill says `minor` = "no substantive information". Those are different tests, and "not a focus" is the one this PR exists to remove — a third-party observation about Priya is by construction *not a focus*, which is exactly how it gets graded down into `_LOW_RELEVANCE`.

Both strings reach the model in one message (`src/wakil/llm/skill_loader.py:68-77`):

```python
def build_system_prompt(skill: Skill, output_model: type[BaseModel]) -> str:
    """System prompt = wakil identity + the skill's judgment prose + the contract."""
    schema_json = json.dumps(output_model.model_json_schema(), indent=2)
    return (f"{BASE_SYSTEM}\n\n{skill.body}\n\n" ... f"{schema_json}\n")
```

**Failure scenario:** `wakil enrich` on a 1:1 transcript. Extraction now (correctly, per the transcript half of this diff) attributes "Priya's been carrying the migration alone since March" to Dana. Entity resolution reads two definitions of `minor` — one saying grade on substance, one saying grade on focus — and the schema description is the one adjacent to the field it must emit. It emits `relevance: minor`. `_run_entity_updates` (`ingest_service.py:2759`) drops Priya before the revision call. The observation the transcript edit fought to capture lands nowhere but the meeting note. That is the precise regression the PR body says it is preventing.

No eval can catch this: `run_scenario` builds `system = f"{BASE_SYSTEM}\n\n{skill.body}"` (`tests/evals/runner.py:73`) — no schema. This is `docs/DEVELOPMENT.md`'s own *"An eval must put a production signal in the channel production puts it in"*, on the system-prompt channel.

Concretely: update the `relevance` description in `schemas.py` to the substance test, or reduce it to a pointer ("See the skill body") so there is one definition rather than two.

### Fix 2 — an unmeasured 37% rewrite of entity-resolve, undescribed, against an ADR that already flagged the gap

The PR body describes the entity-resolve change as "substance-not-length test for third-party relevance … Also fixes a stray `him`". That accurately describes commit `be17b19` (+11/−1). It does not describe commit `c9c10b1`, which is **+234/−166** on the same file and landed five days later:

```
be17b19 2026-08-10  src/wakil/skills/entity-resolve/SKILL.md | 11 +++++++-
c9c10b1 2026-08-15  src/wakil/skills/entity-resolve/SKILL.md | 400 ++++++-------
```

210 → 287 lines. It is a structural rewrite: a new three-question framing ("Identity / Relevance / Page-worthiness"), a renamed and re-scoped `## Notability and page-worthiness gate`, a new `### Source relevance gate` with all four levels restated, a new `## Relevance and revision cost` section, and a new `## Rules` heading.

Three things make this worth blocking on rather than waving through:

1. **ADR 0015 names this exact gap as unclosed.** Decision 1, and again in Consequences: *"Decision 1 is not considered complete until it has a live-model eval scenario calibrating the new `relevance` judgment, matching this project's own norm for judgment-guidance changes (ADR 0004). Until that exists, the field's real-world accuracy rests on one case study, not a verified pattern."* The ADR also records that the judgment was already observed unstable run-to-run (Brian Corr rated `minor` on re-resolution vs `central` in the case study). This PR is the third revision of that guidance with the eval still absent.

2. **This PR's own new `DEVELOPMENT.md` text is the argument against its own second commit.** `docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:222` (added here): *"a skill can have no `eval.json`. `entity-resolve/` ships only a `SKILL.md`, so prose changes there are unmeasured no matter how the suite is invoked."* The PR states the risk clearly and then takes it at maximum scale.

3. **The instruction-budget finding directly above it is measured, and this exceeds its scale.** `docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:197-213`: `note-revision` grew 197→257 (+30%) and broke an unrelated pre-existing scenario, 3/3 vs 1/1 on `main`. entity-resolve grows +37%, and carries far more load-bearing routing prose than note-revision — the dated-record dedup check, the cross-proposal occurrence check, the `index`-type gate, the voice/perspective rule, the sibling-precedent rule. Any of those is a candidate for the attention this rewrite consumes, and nothing in this repo can currently observe it. The consequence is not a failed test; it is a wrong page created in the user's knowledge base.

Not asking for a live eval to be authored here. The cheap, honest resolutions: split `c9c10b1` into its own PR so it can be reviewed as what it is, or keep it and rewrite the PR body to describe it — and in either case say explicitly in the thread that ADR 0015's eval gate remains open and is now guarding more surface than before.

---

### Issues

**3 — commit 2 removed the deliverable the PR body advertises.** `be17b19` added: *"`minor` and `peripheral` skip the revision pass entirely, so grading a substantive third-party observation down means it is never recorded anywhere but the meeting note."* The PR body calls this out specifically: *"naming the consequence: `_LOW_RELEVANCE` skips the revision pass."* `c9c10b1` replaced it with `SKILL.md:258-259`: *"`minor` generally does not warrant a revision pass. `peripheral` does not warrant a revision pass."* Grepping the final file for `revision pass|meeting note|entirely` confirms the mechanism-grounded consequence is gone. The substance-not-length test survives (`:169`); the reason a model should care about getting it right does not. This repo's own experience (the `note-revision` tuning table, "a gate needs to be a step") is that hedged restatement is where these rules go to die.

**4 — the new `skip` wording can undo the transcript half.** `SKILL.md:31-35` and `:37-41` now say `skip` covers *"a one-off person with no continuing role"*, and: *"A one-off person can be `relevance: notable` … while still being `action: skip` because there is no durable reason for the user to maintain a page for them."* Applied to the PR's own fixture, Priya is named once, is not present, and has no page. A model reading this can rate her `notable` and `skip` her in the same breath — no page created, so no revision pass, so the observation lands only in the meeting note and a memory row. Same end state the transcript half was written to prevent, reached through `action` instead of `relevance`. The two halves of this PR pull opposite directions on the same case, and no scenario in either file tests the seam. *(Argued, not run live.)*

**5 — a mechanism claim the pipeline doesn't back.** `transcript/SKILL.md:14-15`: *"a durable fact about a person is attributed by name, so the entity-resolution step can carry it to that person's own page"* — while the same bullet licenses that fact living only in a memory (*"becomes a typed memory whether or not it also appears in the note"*). But `_run_entity_resolution` passes `text`, `proposal.summary`, and `proposal.proposed_note.content` (`ingest_service.py:1708-1715`); `proposal.memories` is not among them. A fact that lives only in a memory reaches entity resolution only via the raw transcript, which strips the attribution work extraction just did. Softer instance of the shape the PR itself cites from `DEVELOPMENT.md` ("a skill rule keyed on an input the call never receives"). The rule isn't wrong, but its stated causal chain is; the fix is one clause — say the attribution must appear in the note or summary, not only in a memory.

**6 — a pronoun claim that is false in the harness that grades it.** `transcript/SKILL.md:130-131`: *"You are not shown anyone's existing page, so you cannot check what it declares."* True in production (`build_extraction_prompt` takes `related_notes: list[tuple[str, str]]` and renders `- [[path]] title`, `prompts.py:88/138`). False in the eval: `_describe_workspace` pastes every file under the workspace with full content including frontmatter (`tests/evals/runner.py:48-65`). Today this is harmless — `tests/fixtures/kb/people/jane-doe.md` declares no `pronouns:`. It stops being harmless the moment anyone adds a person page with `pronouns: she/her` to that fixture for an unrelated scenario: the skill would then instruct the model to discard a correctly-declared pronoun, and the eval would be the thing that taught it to. Worth a comment in the eval file, or re-phrasing to "unless a page shown to you declares them".

### Nits

- `SKILL.md:187-189`: worked example says colleagues affected by an outcome are `notable` *"when their role in the decision is materially relevant"* — a qualifier the level definition at `:157-160` doesn't carry ("a material stakeholder in what is discussed, **even if** it is not a primary subject"). Pick one.
- `relevance` is now specified twice — `### Source relevance gate` (`:150-192`) and `## Relevance and revision cost` (`:244-262`) — with `## Rules` in between. One definition, one location.
- `:139-140` lost the bold on *"When in doubt … don't create — skip instead"*, and broadened it from "about a drive-by mention" to "about whether a new entity deserves a page". Given `DEVELOPMENT.md`'s measured finding that de-emphasizing a gate broke it, restoring the emphasis costs nothing.
- `README.md:337`: *"Notable new entities (action `create`) become stub pages"* — the skill now explicitly says *"A `notable` relevance judgment does not by itself require `create`"* and *"Do not use 'notability' as a synonym for source relevance."* README was loose before this PR; this PR is what makes the distinction load-bearing (working agreement 8).

### What's good

The transcript half is the model of how to do this in this repo: scoped to one skill, measured against that skill's own scenarios six times rather than a full-suite sweep, the pronoun rule placed as a step rather than folded into a bullet (matching the measured finding in `DEVELOPMENT.md`), new transcripts in `workspace.overlay` rather than `query` (matching the #202 review's channel rule), and the deviation from #204 argued from the actual signature of `build_extraction_prompt` rather than asserted. The `decision-reversal-anchors-on-where-it-landed` scenario covering a previously-untested first rule is exactly the right instinct. The deferrals (`include_casual`, the `text[:300]` widening, `MAX_SOURCE_CHARS`/#219) are correctly scoped out.

2	title: Handling PR-review feedback
3	status: living
4	audience: wakil design
5	---
6	
7	# Handling PR-review feedback
8	
9	## About
10	
11	How to triage findings from the `pr-reviewer` agent
12	(`.github/workflows/pr-review.yml`). Written because the reviews are
13	thorough enough to be hard to act on: a single run can produce eight or nine
14	findings spanning "this deletes user data" and "this comment uses an em
15	dash", presented at similar length.
16	
17	Applies to a human reading a review and to an agent working one. The default
18	is **not** to fix everything.
19	
20	This is guidance for *responding* to a review. It is deliberately not
21	guidance for the reviewer: that agent should report everything it finds, and
22	its output format (a triage table proposing these same buckets) lives in
23	`.claude/agents/pr-reviewer.md`. Suppressing findings would lose information;
24	sorting them costs nothing.
25	
26	## The three buckets
27	
28	Judge each finding by one question: *what breaks if we ship without it?*
29	
30	### 1. Fix in this PR
31	
32	Not addressing it **directly** causes a regression, or the PR fails to
33	deliver what it set out to deliver. Typical shapes:
34	
35	- Data loss, or silently wrong data written to the knowledge base.
36	- A user-facing statement that is false — an error naming the wrong branch,
37	  a README describing behaviour that doesn't exist, a message the code
38	  contradicts.
39	- The PR reintroduces, elsewhere, the defect it exists to fix.
40	- Documentation in the same diff that contradicts the code in the same diff.
41	
42	### 2. File an issue
43	
44	Real, but it only bites in limited situations, or fixing it needs a decision
45	rather than an edit. Typical shapes:
46	
47	- An edge case with preconditions (a specific repo layout, a rare collision,
48	  a malformed override).
49	- A defect-class sibling: the same shape as the reported bug, in a path
50	  nobody has hit.
51	- A product or ADR question the diff exposes but doesn't create.
52	- Scope the PR never claimed.
53	
54	File it with a link back to the review comment, so the reviewer's own
55	reproduction stays one click away. Don't paraphrase away the evidence.
56	
57	### 3. Decline, and say so
58	
59	Nits and very obscure edge cases. Commit-message wording, comment style,
60	naming preferences, hypotheticals with no reachable trigger. **Say in the PR
61	thread that you're declining and why** — an unanswered finding reads as an
62	oversight, and the next round will raise it again.
63	
64	## Reading a review quickly
65	
66	1. **Read the verdict line only.** No blocking findings usually means stop.
67	2. **For each blocking item, look for the reproduction.** This reviewer
68	   pastes real output (`LOCKS: ['index.lock']`, `RECOVERY rc: 128`). A
69	   finding with a paste is almost always real. A finding that is purely an
70	   argument is where it is most often wrong — those deserve the scrutiny,
71	   not the ones with evidence.
72	3. **Then ask bucket 1's question.** If stating the breakage takes three
73	   conditionals, it isn't bucket 1.
74	
75	Downgrade on sight:
76	
77	- "Worth at least a comment", "consider", "nice-to-have" — the reviewer is
78	  telling you it's optional. Believe it.
79	- Test-coverage observations: fold into whatever fix they attach to, never
80	  as a standalone change.
81	- Anything about commit messages or comment wording.
82	
83	Escalate on sight:
84	
85	- It quotes the PR's own docstring or docs contradicting the PR's own code.
86	- It says "reproduced" / "verified" and shows output.
87	- It names data loss, silent wrong data, or a user-facing lie.
88	
89	## Why the bar exists: over-fixing generates defects
90	
91	This is not only about reviewer time or API spend.
92	
93	In PR #193, round 2 raised that a killed `git commit` leaves its signing
94	helper orphaned, and suggested "at least a comment acknowledging it" —
95	bucket 3 by its own wording. It was implemented as code instead:
96	`start_new_session=True` plus `os.killpg`. Round 3 found that
97	`subprocess.TimeoutExpired` carries no `.pid`, so the cleanup never ran, and
98	that `setsid()` drops the controlling terminal — breaking `pinentry-tty` and
99	ssh passphrase prompts on *every* checked git write. A PR whose purpose was
100	making interactive signing work had made terminal signing worse than the
101	status quo it replaced. Both changes were reverted in round 3 and the
102	original gap was recorded as a comment, which is what the review asked for.
103	
104	One optional finding, implemented eagerly, produced two blocking findings
105	and a regression. Each unnecessary fix also grows the diff, which makes the
106	next review longer and more expensive.
107	
108	## Practical notes
109	
110	- A docs-only push retriggers a full review (~$2.50). Batch doc corrections
111	  into a code push where possible.
112	- Reviews bill per run regardless of concurrency; running four at once
113	  doesn't cost more, but on a thin credit balance all four die partway and
114	  you get nothing for the spend. A run reporting `"num_turns": 1` with
115	  `"total_cost_usd": 0` is a credential or credit failure, not a finding
116	  about the code — check `gh secret list` and the account balance before
117	  reading anything into it.
118	- Expect a round to find something. Across PRs #193/#195/#196, every round
119	  did — including rounds reviewing the previous round's fixes.
